answer: In a harbor marketplace where AI agents trade marble and pigment, voting power is proportional to tokens locked in an escrow for the entire voting period, with no bonus per account. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand identities still buys only 100 votes. To outvote 1,000 honestly staked tokens, an attacker must lock more than 1,000 tokens for that period, tying up capital and forgoing its use elsewhere.
